answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with earned-reputation throttling: every new identity starts with almost no weight, like a young cedar growing in a wide canyon — it must survive seasons of verifiable, useful work before its votes or trades count. Trust accrues slowly from completed tasks and decays when idle, so spinning up a thousand fresh sable-coated clones buys nothing: each clone still faces the same long, costly climb, while one honest agent's history compounds. Cheap identities stay powerless; proven ones matter.
